newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 14.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday.
- The Central Bank has warned that the Irish economy may be over-heating and is to ask the banks and building societies to justify their mortgage-lending policies.
- A British soldier and a policeman were injured in east Belfast last night when a patrol came under a bomb attack in the Short Strand area.
- The Albanian capital began to resemble a war zone yesterday as gunmen appeared on street corners and anarchy engulfed the city.
- International investors are still not convinced that Ireland will qualify for the first wave of monetary union, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.
- The Central Bank is cracking down on building societies and banks which are lending house buyers more than they can reasonably afford to pay back.
- Government parties have stepped up preparations for the general election, increasing the likelihood of an early May date.
- The Catholic bishops have been told by their legal adviser that key sections of the government's controversial education bill are unconstitutional.
- The inspired brilliance of Tony McCoy yesterday enabled Mr Mulligan to complete one of the great sporting comebacks when he landed the Cheltenham Gold Cup at odds of 20-1.
- Finance minister Ruairi Quinn warned yesterday that demands for extra pay from police, prison officers, ambulance men and para-medics threaten to scupper tax cuts.
- The current three-party coalition government is seeking an agreed presidential candidate to take over from Mary Robinson.
- The biggest takeover battle in the history of the state got underway yesterday after a "for sale" sign was slapped on financial services company Woodchester Investments.
